4.08 Vegetation Resource. Because the construction site has been previously excavated, there should be virtually no impact upon the vegetative resource if reasonable construction procedures are followed.
4.09 Esthetic Resource. Although the present environmental setting is far from wilderness, the introduction and activity of construction equipment will slightly detract and diminish the present scenic values.
4.10 Recreation. Recreation at Amistad Reservoir should not be significantly affected by construction activities. Although the construction area is not presently utilized for recreation activities, traffic associated with the construction program may result in temporary inconvenience to tourists or other recreationists.
4.11 Fish and Wildlife Resources. Although wildlife in the construction area would be disturbed by noise, dust, and human activity, the disturbance would be short-termed. Limited inorganic sediments could be carried into surface waters of the stilling basin and river as a result of construction activities and runoff. Deposition of this inert material could affect the habitat of benthic invertebrates and might smother some of the less mobile organisms. Adult and juvenile fishes should not be adversely affected by the loss of benthic organisms. They should be able to survive any environmental stress as a result of localized turbidity and sedimentation. Environmental stresses could cause certain fish species to become more susceptible to disease and parasite infestations.
4.12 Construction of the powerhouse will result in a small loss of aquatic habitat within the stilling basin. This effect is not considered a significant impact upon the fishery's resource and its habitat since the aquatic habitat was created as a result of earlier excavation for the powerhouse. The construction impact upon the fish and wildlife resource is not considered significant.
4.13 Historical and Archeological Resources. There will be no adverse impacts to archeological and historical resources since there are none located within the construction area.
4.14 Socioeconomic Consideration. The socioeconomic effect in the immediate area of the project should be relatively small compared to construction in a populous or developed region. The proposed action will, however, require a commitment of capital, labor, and natural resources which will preclude their use for other projects.
4.15 The number of construction workers accociated with the project will vary by season and by year; employment will generally increase. Wages earned will be spent in nearby retail and service establishments. The local economy is also expected to benefit from the purchase of construction materials and supplies. Although the local communities will benefit from construction, there will be unavoidable but temporary adverse effects. The influx of construction workers and their families will impact the local community, especially their demand for services including housing and education. There will be other effects which include increases in traffic, noise, congestion, etc., that come from being the closest population center to a construction site.
